title: Princess
text: It had been less than an hour since we left the village in the east. The carriage was moving slowly toward the town below Melromarc Castle. We still have plenty of time, after all. There’s no need to rush.
“Naofumi!”
But after we’d gone a little further, Sakura-chan called out to her Father.
“What’s the matter, Sakura-chan?”
“You know, that archer who fought Naofumi at the castle before is walking toward us.”
“Yikes!”

Father looked out the window and let out a cry. When I looked as well, I saw Itsuki and his party walking along with their companions. I wondered if the Crimson Swine was there, but they were too far away to tell for sure.

Itsuki himself was dressed rather plainly. Does he usually dress like that? With a sword strapped to his waist, he’s probably just pretending to be an ordinary adventurer. I wish they’d come a little closer, but my Father says to Sakura-chan in a flustered tone:

“If Itsuki, the Saint of the Divine Bird, finds out we’re the ones, who knows what he’ll say. It’d be a hassle if he picks a fight with us. Can’t you use a transformation to cover it up, like Luna-chan does?”
“Hmm? Got it!”
With that, Sakura-chan transforms from her Queen form into her Filolial form and starts pulling the carriage. Yuki-chan and the others followed suit.
“Everyone, try not to make a sound, okay?”
“Got it, big bro. That guy with the bow’s only being rude to us, anyway.”
Keel’s right. Well, since Itsuki is under the Crimson Swine’s influence, I guess it can’t be helped. Just then, the Assistant who had been flying through the sky on his Rival’s back landed and asked:
“What’s that?”
“It’s the Bow Hero and his party. To be honest, they’re a more troublesome bunch than the Sword Hero—if they spot us. Wyndia and Gaelion, just stay quiet, okay?”
“Got it.”

The assistant then discreetly mounted Rival and soared high into the sky. After that, holding our breath, my Father and I passed right by Itsuki and the others, who were chatting and laughing with their companions. We got through without any trouble—no one paid us any special attention.
Still, the Crimson Swine wasn’t with them, as expected. I wonder if he’s living it up at the castle or something.
“Phew… We managed to pull it off somehow.”
“It didn’t seem like they noticed.”
“Well, as long as that’s the case. Hopefully, they just thought we were a traveling merchant’s wagon or something. By the way… I wonder where the group was headed?”
My father looked from the back of the wagon toward the receding figures of the group, who were already far away. Where is Itsuki headed?
“That’s the village to the east… or maybe they’re heading toward the border?”
“Unfortunately, I have no idea.”
“Hmm… maybe it was a good thing we left the village early. If Itsuki had shown up, who knows what he’d have said… It’d be a nightmare if he accused us of spreading the plague.”
My father muttered under his breath. Well, it’s Itsuki, after all. At first glance, he’ll side with the poor, innocent victim.
“Is that the Bow Hero?”
The assistant came down with his Rival and asked.
“Yeah. His name is Itsuki Kawasumi, the Bow Hero. He seems to have a strong sense of justice, but honestly, he’s probably just self-satisfied and selfish.”
With a distant look in her eyes, the assistant gazed in the direction Itsuki had gone. She has extraordinary feelings for Ren, the Sword Hero, after all. She must have her own thoughts about heroes.
“If the Bow Hero had arrived at the village before us… I wonder what would have happened to Dad and the village?”
“Hmm… Ju has the same skills as us, after all. As a result, the village might have been saved.”
“…I see.”
“But I think there was meaning in us arriving first.”
“Yeah, I got to exchange a few words with Dad. Just that alone… means a lot to me.”
With that, the Assistant flashed a gentle smile and ruffled Rival’s head.
“Gau!”
Rival let out a happy-sounding cry. Wait, is this actually the Assistant’s monster, not Rival? To keep things simple, let’s just call it “Rival” from now on. “Well then,” said my Father.
“I panicked when I saw Itsuki, but if it’s just a quick errand, I can manage with my portal skill, right?”
“That’s right.”
“Deciding on a meeting spot and moving quickly isn’t a bad idea, is it?”
“Are you moving, big bro?”
“Where are you going?”
The Assistant asked.
“To the town below Melromarc Castle—and while I’m there, I’ll talk to the Sword Hero…”

Just as I muttered that, the Assistant and the Rival’s expressions darkened. Well, from the Assistant’s perspective, he’s the killer of her parent, and from the Rival’s, he’s the one who killed her. It’s only natural they’d react that way.
“I’m not going.”
“…Well, I suppose so. Then, Wyndia-chan, I’ll ask you and Gaelion-chan to mind the place while I’m gone.”
“Okay.”
Just then, I heard Filolial-sama’s cry from afar. I leaned out of the carriage and scanned the area.
“Ah… I wonder if wild Filolials live around here?”
“That might very well be the case!”

Come to think of it, there are Filolial habitats in Melromarc. Wild Filolial-samas are quite a sight to behold in their own right. They have a leaner, more toned build than the Filolial-samas raised by humans. No matter what kind of Filolial-sama it is, I’ll love it.
“Motoyasu-sama has such a deep love.”
“Kitamura’s eyes are sparkling!”
“Piyo?”
“Come to think of it, I can smell a Filolial-sama… Well, I didn’t notice because of everyone else’s scent.”
“After all, there are quite a few Filolials among our group…”
My Father is looking at me with an exasperated expression. Just then, I spotted a flock of Filolial-samas in the distance.

It seems they’ve spotted us and are letting out warning cries. Please wait, Filolial-samas—we mean you no harm. “Please come over here—just be yourselves.” But my hopes were in vain; the Filolial-samas sprinted away at full speed.
“Father, should we try chasing after those wild Filolial-samas?”
“What’s the point of doing that? They’ll probably hate it, too.”
Hmm, now that you mention it, you’re right. I thought we could become friends if we just interacted with them.

“Come to think of it, there aren’t as many wild Filolial-samas as you’d expect, are there? I’ve seen all sorts of things in Siltvelt and Melromarc, but this might be the first time I’ve ever seen one.”
“Hmm?”
“We’re not so tactless as to trample into someone else’s territory without good reason.”
“Exactly!”
Sakura-chan tilted her head, and Yuki-chan and the others declared proudly.
“More importantly, Motoyasu-sama! Please look at us instead of the wild Filolials.”
“I’m looking at all of you.”
Ah, the wild Filolial-sama have already disappeared from view.
“Motoyasu-sama…”
For some reason, Yuki-chan has a distant look in her eyes and is reaching out toward me. So I gently stroked Yuki-chan’s head.
“She’s at that age where she wants to be pampered, isn’t she? Hahaha.”
“Um… I don’t think that’s what Yuki-chan meant.”
“Pet Kou too!”
“Sure thing.”

I petted Kou as well, since he was being so affectionate. Then Yuki-chan puffed out her cheeks and got sulky. What’s the matter? Ah, she’s feeling jealous because her parent is doting on her sibling. What an adorable reaction.
“Hmph…”

For some reason, the Lazy Pig was shaking his head as if to say, “Oh, come on.” Just as we were enjoying this cheerful conversation, a group approached the carriage. They rode alongside it and called out to us.
“Hello there!”
“Hm?”
Father tilted his head and signaled for Keel to respond.
“What is it?”
“It appears to be the carriage of the Holy One of the Divine Bird. We humbly request an audience with our princess.”

I peeked my head out from under the carriage canopy just a little to look at them. There, I saw a knight from Melromarc, who seemed to be leading a carriage of some sort. Is the “princess” they’re referring to Crimson Swine? Depending on the situation, it might be better to refuse. My Father glanced at me once and nodded, then pulled his robe tightly around himself before leaning out of the carriage.
“So the princess—such a distinguished figure—is willing to speak with us, is she?”
“That’s right. You should consider it an honor beyond your station.”
What a high-handed attitude. I could just blow that princess—and Crimson Swine—right out of here on the spot.
“So? What kind of person is this princess? I’d like to know her name.”
“Hear it and be in awe. She is none other than the Second Princess of Melromarc, Lady Melty Merlomark.”
